text:
maya: Quick thought — we need to nail the semantics of "activation quorum" for on‑prem package apply. current doc says 'majority of components', but that doesn't map well to operator-managed components.
chris: Agreed. Majority of what? pods? nodes? registered components?
zane: My vote: quorum should be defined over 'activation voters' that are explicit entries in the manifest. that way operator can add/remove voters for specific deployments.
ida: +1 to explicit voters. also need a grace_period after quorum where late activations are accepted but flagged. otherwise transient network blips cause unnecessary rollbacks.
maya: proposal: two params in manifest: activation_quorum: {required: N, voters: [a,b,c]} and activation_grace_seconds: 900. semantics: once N voters report activation, system marks package active but continues to accept reports until grace window closes. late reporters are recorded as 'late' and can trigger alerts.
chris: sounds reasonable. edge: what if a voter never reports because it's decommissioned but still listed? do we have a fallback?
zane: add 'voter_tombstone' flag controlled by operator. but we should also support automatic tombstone if voter hasn't appeared in X deploy cycles.
rebecca: ops concern: automatic tombstone is scary for compliance customers. they want explicit audit trail and manual tombstone via the console.
ida: fair. default should be manual; automatic tombstone can be opt‑in via cluster policy.
maya: typo: maya.
maya: (lol) fixed. back to flow — we also need a clear rollback trigger: if quorum falls below threshold during the grace window, do we auto-rollback or enter 'degraded-active' state?
zane: prefer 'degraded-active' with explicit operator action to rollback. automatic rollback can be catastrophic for on‑prem customers.
chris: agree. degraded-active should 1) route traffic off components that dropped, 2) emit an incident, 3) expose a single 'reconcile' action in console.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: observed pattern: in 3/12 recent onprem upgrades, nodes flaked for ~5m after activation. recommend default grace_seconds=600 for stability.
rebecca: ops-bot data matches our support logs. 600s seems fine for most infra, but add a per‑manifest override.
maya: implementation notes: runtime needs to collect activation receipts signed by local agent, with a short-lived nonce to prevent replay. receipts get replicated to control-plane audit log. sample receipt format: ```
{
  "voter_id": "node-42",
  "package_id": "pkg-2026-03-xx",
  "activated_at": "2026-03-22T01:02:03Z",
  "nonce": "abc123",
  "sig": "..."
}
```
ida: receipts + audit log solves a lot of trust questions. also add a 'state_transition_event' stream so SREs can hook anomaly detection.
zane: interactions with offline installers: if control-plane is unreachable, local operator should still allow activation when local quorum achieved among voters on the same airgapped cluster, but mark package as 'locally-active' and queue replication when control-plane comes back.
chris: that behaviour needs an explicit allow_local_activation flag in manifest. otherwise we risk split-brain between clusters that will replicate later.
maya: agreed. manifest fields summary: activation_quorum: {required, voters}, activation_grace_seconds, allow_local_activation (bool, default false), tombstone_policy {manual|auto|policy-optional}.
rebecca: rollout UX: console should show a compact timeline: quorum reached -> grace window -> late reporters -> finalize or reconcile. customers ask for a one-click 'force-finalize' to close the window. include audit reason text when clicked.
ida: security: receipts signed via KMS or local key; rotation policy must be in docs. receipts older than retention window are prunable.
ops-bot: note: metric hooks: gauge(active_voters), counter(late_reporters), histogram(grace_window_latency).
maya: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with the manifest schema, sample receipts, and operator UX flows. want reviewers: chris, zane, rebecca, ida.
chris: I'll review. focus on failure modes around partial network partitions.
zane: I'll add test scenarios (simulated flaky nodes, missing voters, manual tombstone flow).
rebecca: forwarding to support playbook owners for runbook additions.
ida: ping me when RFC is up, I'll add KMS rotation text.
maya: thanks all. :thumbsup:
